cards.text: The apostle Paul is writing to the church in Corinth about a generous gift they promised for the saints. He's been bragging to the Macedonians that they're ready, so he's sending some brothers ahead to make sure. Friend, this is a man who told EVERYBODY you're bringing the cookies, and now he's checking in. Twice.
Now Paul grabs a picture every farmer knows: you sow seed, then you reap the harvest. I planted a chocolate chip once, friend, and I am STILL waiting.

cards.question: In Paul's farming picture, what happens to the one who sows sparingly?
True or false: Paul says whoever sows generously will also reap generously.

cards.text: So how much should each one give? Paul's not running a toll booth, friend. Each one gives what he has decided in his heart to give.

cards.question: Each one gives what he has decided in his heart, not out of regret or ___.
Then Paul gives the reason for giving from the heart. What kind of giver does God love?

cards.text: Cheerful. So no handing over the cookie box with a face like the alarm just went off at 4 a.m. And Paul says God is able to make all grace abound to you.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says giving like this will leave the Corinthians short on what they need.

cards.text: Then Paul backs it up with Scripture, a line from Psalm 112:9 about gifts scattered abroad. And it ends with righteousness that endures forever.

cards.question: In the line Paul quotes, He has scattered abroad His gifts to the ___.

cards.text: Back to the farm. Paul says God is the One who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food, and friend, the One handing out the seed is NOT about to run out of seed.

cards.question: God supplies the sower with seed. What does Paul say God will do with the Corinthians' store of seed?
Paul says God will also increase the harvest of their ___.

cards.text: God enriches them in every way, so they can be generous on every occasion. That's me with a fresh batch, friend: those cookies are NOT for Papa.

cards.question: Through Paul and his team, what will the Corinthians' generosity produce?
True or false: Paul says this service only supplies the needs of the saints and does nothing more.
When the saints see the proof of the Corinthians' generous gift, what will they do?

cards.text: And the saints will pray for the Corinthians with affection, because of the surpassing grace God has given them. You give a gift and get PRAYED for? Best deal since somebody bought me for twenty-five cents.

cards.question: Paul can't hold it in. He ends with thanks be to God for His ___ gift!

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'The apostle Paul is writing…', 'He's been bragging…', 'Friend, this is a man who…', and 'Twice.'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

findings.problem: The opening card gives context from the previous passage and cites 2 Corinthians 9:1-5, which is outside this passage (9:6-15). The reveal screen shows the verses the passage has covered so far, so this citation may put 9:1-5 on the reveal screen.
findings.question: When the opening card gives context from the passage before, should it cite those outside verses, cite the first verse of this passage, or cite nothing?

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'So how much should each one give?', 'Paul's not running a toll booth, friend.', and 'Each one gives what he has decided in his heart to give.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank follows 'not out of regret or', so it needs a negative word. 'compulsion' is the only negative choice, and 'joy' and 'faith' are positive. The wrong answers don't fit the sentence, so the right answer stands out. Also, no earlier card sets up 'regret or compulsion', so the card asks the baker to finish the wording of the line.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Cheerful.', 'So no handing over the cookie box…', and 'And Paul says God is able to make all grace abound to you.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Verse 8 says why God makes grace abound: 'you will abound in every good work.' No card tells or asks about this. It is the point of the verse.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the wording 'harvest of your ___'. The story card before it sets up only seed and bread, so 'fields' is the natural reasoned pick. 'righteousness' can only be guessed from the wording, or picked up from card 10's unrelated mention of righteousness.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Verse 13 says the saints glorify God for the Corinthians' 'obedient confession of the gospel of Christ' as well as for their generosity. No card mentions the obedient confession of the gospel, so the baker misses half of what the saints glorify God for.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'And the saints will pray…', 'You give a gift and get PRAYED for?', and 'Best deal since…'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke calls back to Papa Dorin being bought for twenty-five cents. That setup never comes earlier in this lesson, and the line doesn't say what it refers to. Bakers are only known to know about the junk drawer from onboarding.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: The question has the baker guess the exact adjective in Paul's closing line (indescribable, earthly or first). No earlier card gives anything to reason from, so it is pure wording guesswork.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: 'Paul can't hold it in.' states Paul's feeling as fact. The text gives no feeling here, and the line isn't marked as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.
